annotations.text:
PHOSPHOR
Operator console. Monospace throughout, hairline rules, corner ticks, scanline texture, phosphor-green accent with a real glow. The GUI sibling of the Bubble Tea TUI — bracketed key hints, a status line on top and a keymap bar on the bottom.

Strongest identity of the three, and the densest.

Tradeoff: the CRT metaphor is dark-native. See the light-mode board at the bottom before committing.

SUBSTRATE
The restrained one. System sans for chrome, mono for every piece of data. Cards, 8px radii, one indigo accent, soft shadows. Closest to Linear / Vercel / the Tailscale admin console.

Will age best and is the least risky to port — it is roughly where the app already is, done properly.

Tradeoff: nothing about it is memorable. It looks like every other dev tool, which may be exactly what you want.

MERIDIAN
Geography as the organising idea. The band across the top plots each node at its REAL longitude and latitude — fra1 sits east of nyc1 because Frankfurt is east of New York, and all three sit north because your whole fleet is in the northern mid-latitudes. Not decoration: it is a fact about your fleet you cannot get from the table.

The datacenter picker carries the same motif — each card shows where in the world that region is.

Tradeoff: the band costs ~150px of vertical space and earns it at 3 nodes, less so at 20. It could collapse once the table gets long.

The same Phosphor dashboard inverted to light.

The scanlines and glow are gone — they cannot survive a white ground — so what remains is the layout and the hairline discipline. It holds up, but it stops being a CRT and becomes a plain dense table.

Worth deciding deliberately: Phosphor could ship dark-only and ignore the OS preference, which is defensible for a tool like this and is what the app does NOT do today.

Three directions, same three screens, same real data. Compare across a row for one direction; compare down a column to see how each direction handles the same screen.

All three use system font stacks only and draw every icon as inline SVG or a CSS shape, so whichever wins ports into the single-file app with no assets and no build step.

TVA
Phosphor's bones in the Time Variance Authority palette: amber P3 phosphor on warm near-black, cream text, tan hairlines, olive and brick-rust indicator lamps. Amber is the interactive colour; healthy nodes read olive so the four states stay distinguishable instead of collapsing into one hue.

CONSOLE (left) puts the screen inside the beige housing — silkscreened labels, indicator lamps, printed key legends on the lower rail, a prompt cursor on the screen itself. Furthest from a normal web app, closest to the workstation.

SCREEN ONLY (right) is the same recolour with no housing — all screen, like a terminal filling the window.

Tradeoff: the console frame spends ~90px of height on chrome that carries no data, and the beige is a commitment. The flat one gives that height back to the table.

The sign-in matches the app as it now stands: ONE credentials field holding both tokens, with the two-token helper collapsed beneath it. No proxy URL — the relay is served from the same origin.
